rationale: Lycopolitan variant of standard Sahidic ⲥϣⲉ 'it is fitting, it is right.' Construction ⲥⲱⲉ ⲁ-PERSON ⲁ-VERB 'fitting for X to do Y' matches the Sahidic deontic pattern. Vowel-form ⲱ for ϣⲉ may be dialectal.
Greek loanword πείθεσθαι 'be persuaded.' Used here reflexively with ϩⲙ̄ ⲡⲉϩϩⲏⲧ 'in his heart' = persuasive conviction in the heart.
Reduplicated verbal form, possibly Lyc reflex of ϫⲱⲡϫⲡ̄ 'crush, trample.' Restored from the editor's bracket [ⲭⲁⲡ]ⲭⲡ; fits context of treading on the Cross of Light.

From verbal root ⲣⲱⲧ 'grow, sprout, take root' (cf. accumulated ⲣⲍⲱⲧ ⲛⲍⲏⲧϩ 'be rooted/established'). Substantival 'a growing-thing, a sprout' — the hidden Light-element emerging in its earliest vegetative stage.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣⲟⲟⲩϣ 'care, anxiety, concern.' Used here for the brethren's pastoral concern that the disciple bears with him on his journey.
Lycopolitan reduced form of ⲟⲩⲱⲛ 'open,' here in the dialogue-introduction idiom 'opened (his mouth) to the Apostle' = 'addressed the Apostle.' Standard Coptic dialogue formula.
